do.name: Hillwalk the Glen Coe ridges
do.detail: Bidean nam Bian, Buachaille Etive Mor and the knife edge Aonach Eagach rise straight off the glen road.

do.name: The 1692 massacre, told on site
do.detail: The visitor centre and the walk to Signal Rock set out what happened to the MacDonalds that February.

do.name: The Lost Valley
do.detail: Coire Gabhail, where the MacDonalds hid stolen cattle. Up a dried riverbed with a little scrambling, about an hour and a quarter, and the valley floor opens out flat and hidden at the top.

do.name: The Three Sisters
do.detail: Beinn Fhada, Gearr Aonach and Aonach Dubh drop their buttresses straight onto the A82, and the roadside viewpoint looks up all three at once.

do.name: Ski and board at Glencoe Mountain
do.detail: Scotland's oldest ski ground sits on Meall a Bhuiridh, with lessons, hire and sledging when snow holds.

do.name: A night at the Clachaig Inn
do.detail: The climbers' bar in the glen, with local ales, boots by the fire and live music on many weekends.

do.name: Find the film locations
do.detail: The glen and Glen Etive stood in for Bond country and for Hogwarts hillsides, and guides run the circuit.

do.name: Chairlift up and bike down
do.detail: The lift carries riders and walkers to the plateau cafe, with downhill trails and hire bikes at the base.

do.name: Devil's Staircase on the West Highland Way
do.detail: The long walk crosses the head of the glen and zigzags over the pass down to Kinlochleven.

do.name: National Trust visitor centre
do.detail: Off the A82 at the east end of the glen: the geology, the wildlife and the massacre in one exhibition, plus trail maps for the walks and a cafe.
